# Quickstart — first time teaching this course

You are teaching **ENGR-3027 Process Engineering** for the Fanshawe College EMN
program: second-year electromechanical / mechanical engineering technology
students heading into automotive, food and defence. The course doubles as a
Quarto book (this repo) that students read as lecture notes.

::: {.callout-note}
**Scope of this handbook.** The student book (`30-Labs.qmd`, chapter 19) is a
**catalogue of labs identified by name** — more labs than one term can deliver,
picked to suit the instructor's background and the equipment available. This
handbook covers the **default 14-week plan** the current offering runs, plus the
prep, keys, rubrics and fallbacks for the **other catalogue labs** (metrology,
statistical quality control, materials testing, virtual welding). Two constraints
govern any selection — the **machine-learning labs are a set** and the **three
materials labs are a 3-week rotation that needs dry ice ordered two weeks ahead**
(§12–13).
:::

**The shape of the default plan (14 weeks):**

- **One lab per week.** The labs scheduled in weeks 1–12 are mandatory to pass;
  the two in weeks 13–14 (TPM/OEE, Root Cause & a New Dataset; Robotic Work-Cell
  Design) are graded but not mandatory.
- **Week 7 is midterm week.** The midterm is written in *lecture* time, so the
  week-7 lab period runs as normal — ML Week 1 is scheduled there
  deliberately because it is the lightest lab in the plan.
- **Weeks 7–12 are the six-week machine-learning module** (2 h theory + 2 h lab per
  week), paired with Chapter 21.
- **Robotic Work-Cell Design is take-home**: released in week 11 (alongside ML
  Week 5), due at the end of week 14, with a short screen recording.
- **Week 14** also holds the final test (lecture time) and a make-up lab slot.

**Hard constraint on the labs in the default plan:** browser-only. No robots, no PLCs, no lab
hardware, no software installs beyond what is already on the lab image
(Microsoft Office / Project / Visio for the Design Documentation and Facility
Design labs, AnyLogic PLE for the latter). The catalogue's metrology, materials
and welding labs do need equipment and rooms — see §6 and §12–13.
Everything else runs in a browser on the free tier.

**What is committed vs. not:**

- Committed: the book (`*.qmd`), `R/make_lab_data.R`, this handbook.
- Not committed (stage on FOL each term): all lab datasets, all notebooks, all
  templates. `R/make_lab_data.R` regenerates the two seeded CSVs.
- Grade weights live in **FOL only**. The student book carries policy and a
  schedule, never weight numbers. This handbook carries a grade-*item* checklist
  (no weights) so FOL can be verified.

**Before week 1, in order:**

1. Read this whole document.
2. Run `Rscript R/make_lab_data.R` and stage the two CSVs on FOL (§7).
3. Walk the software / firewall checklist (§10) from the *college network*.
4. Verify the FOL grade book against the grade-item checklist (§3).
5. Confirm the term grid (§2) against what the program actually timetables — the
   chapter→week mapping is a reconstruction, not the college's own sequence.

# AI-use policy

Mirrored from the student book (`index.qmd`, "Use of generative AI"). Fanshawe
policy A136 permits generative AI only with prior instructor consent; the table
below **is** that consent, per assessment. If an assessment is not listed, treat
it as **not permitted**. Where AI is permitted or required, the student must be
able to explain every line submitted; where permitted with disclosure, they add
a one-line note naming the tool and use.

| Assessment | AI use | Why |
|-----------|--------|-----|
| Logic Thinking (Rocksi) | Not permitted | The outcome *is* their own logic |
| Engineering Design Process Documentation | Not permitted | Already stated in the lab |
| Facility Design & Simulation (AnyLogic) | Not permitted | Already stated in the lab |
| Lean: Value Stream Mapping, Takt and Pull | Permitted with disclosure | Not for the map or the takt/PCE calculations |
| Ergonomics (REBA) | Permitted with disclosure | Not for the REBA scoring itself |
| SPC & Gauge R&R: the Virtual Caliper | Not permitted for readings/calculations; permitted to check the written reflection | The student is the measurement system being studied |
| Machine-learning labs (all six) | Required | Assessed on directing an LLM well, not on writing Python |
| TPM/OEE, Root Cause & a New Dataset | Required for the classifier task; permitted with disclosure elsewhere | Same skill, unfamiliar dataset |
| Robotic Work-Cell Design (RoboDK) | Permitted with disclosure | The station, program and cycle times must be their own |
| Metrology, statistical-quality-control and materials-testing labs (all) | Not permitted for readings, calculations and graphs; written answers must be the student's own | The data and analysis are the assessment. *Proposed default — the source handouts do not state a policy; the student book must list any lab you deliver.* |
| Virtual-welding labs (all six) | Not applicable | Hands-on in the simulator |
| Assignments 1–6 | Permitted with disclosure | — |
| Pop quizzes, midterm, final | Not permitted | Closed-book, in-person |

Each lab's `.lab-overview` in the book restates its own AI status so a student
reading one lab does not have to go back to `index.qmd`. Keep the two in sync.

# Data generation

Run once per term, from the repo root:

```
Rscript R/make_lab_data.R
```

It is base-R only, fully `set.seed()`-ed, and:

**Writes to `./lab_data/`** (gitignored — never commit; stage on FOL):

| File | Lab | Contents | FOL folder |
|------|-----|----------|-----------|
| `vsm_station_data.csv` | Lean VSM | 5 stations × (cycle time, changeover, uptime, WIP, batch size, value-added flag) | Lean VSM materials |
| `precitech_shift_log.csv` | TPM/OEE | 5 days × (planned time, breakdown/setup/small-stop minutes, ideal cycle time, counts, scrap) | TPM/OEE materials |

**Prints** the answer keys reproduced in §8. Re-running the script produces
byte-identical CSVs and identical keys, so a key printed once stays valid for
every term until the generator is changed.

The Virtual Caliper data and its SPC dataset are generated **inside the webR
cells** in `30-Labs.qmd`, not written to a file — the script reproduces their
seeding so you have the ground truth for marking.

The AI4I 2020 dataset (TPM/OEE lab) is **not** generated — students download it from
UCI in the browser. Host a copy on FOL as a firewall fallback.

# Answer keys

Regenerate any time with `Rscript R/make_lab_data.R`. Values below are from the
committed generator.

## Lean VSM

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Available time / shift | 26 400 s (7.33 h; 8 h − two 20-min breaks) |
| **Takt time** | **105.6 s/kit** (250 kits/day) |
| **Bottleneck** | **CNC turn** — C/T 120 s, the only station above takt |
| Stations with spare capacity | Deburr (74 s), Wash (40 s), Inspect (58 s), Kitting (96 s) |
| Value-added time | 216 s (CNC turn + Kitting) |
| Production lead time | ≈ 97 540 s ≈ 27.1 h (Little's law on total WIP 930 units) |
| **Process cycle efficiency** | **≈ 0.22 %** (VA time ÷ lead time) — typical for batch flow |

A future state that halves the CNC-turn changeover and replaces one push link
with a supermarket should cut WIP and lead time materially; accept any
defensible ladder that recomputes consistently.

## Virtual Caliper

Seed `set.seed(3027)`; `caliper_ref <- round(sort(runif(10, 24.90, 25.10)), 3)`;
`caliper_bias <- 0.03 + 0.05*(caliper_ref - 25.00)`.

| Part | Certified reference (mm) | Gauge bias at that size (mm) |
|------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | 24.932 | +0.0266 |
| 2 | 24.948 | +0.0274 |
| 3 | 24.963 | +0.0282 |
| 4 | 24.972 | +0.0286 |
| 5 | 25.022 | +0.0311 |
| 6 | 25.029 | +0.0314 |
| 7 | 25.035 | +0.0318 |
| 8 | 25.049 | +0.0324 |
| 9 | 25.058 | +0.0329 |
| 10 | 25.070 | +0.0335 |

- **Mean gauge bias ≈ +0.030 mm**, rising slightly with size (that is the
  linearity signal — slope ≈ +0.05 mm bias per mm of size, ≈ 0.007 mm over the
  study range).
- **Gauge R&R (indicative):** with modest reading error the simulator gives
  %GRR ≈ 23 %, ndc ≈ 6. Expect student results in the **20–35 % (marginal)**
  band with **ndc ≈ 4–6**; sloppier reading pushes %GRR past 30 % and ndc below
  5. The 0.05 mm resolution against a ±0.05 mm tolerance is the reason the gauge
  is at best marginal — that is the Task 6 lesson.
- **Seeded X̄/R + Cpk dataset** (`set.seed(250)`, 25 subgroups × 5):
  X̄̄ ≈ 25.0082, R̄ ≈ 0.0255, σ̂ ≈ 0.0110 mm; X̄ limits ≈ [24.9935, 25.0229];
  **Cp ≈ 1.52, Cpk ≈ 1.27** (below the 1.33 Tier-1 bar). Subgroups **12–16** are
  beyond 3σ — a seeded special-cause shift. Students should also flag the
  run-of-8 and 2-of-3 patterns entering and leaving that excursion.

## TPM/OEE, Root Cause & a New Dataset

From `precitech_shift_log.csv` (`set.seed(1213)`, 5 days):

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Availability | ≈ 83.2 % |
| Performance | ≈ 94.2 % |
| Quality | ≈ 95.9 % |
| **Weekly OEE** | **≈ 75.1 %** |
| **Dominant Big Loss** | **Breakdowns** (≈ 177 min), then Setup & adjustment (≈ 124 min), then Reduced speed (≈ 107 min) |

**AI4I 2020 failure-mode Pareto** (known dataset, ≈ 339 machine failures in
10 000 rows): HDF ≈ OSF ≈ PWF (the vital few) **>** TWF **>** RNF. RNF is
injected noise — it must be excluded from corrective action. Failure rate
≈ **3.4 %**, so **accuracy is a useless metric**; require precision/recall (and a
class-weight or resampling fix). A team that reports 96 %+ accuracy and stops has
missed the entire point of the lab.

## Robotic Work-Cell Design (RoboDK)

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Takt time (from the Lean VSM lab) | 105.6 s/kit |
| Expected first working cycle time | ≈ 12–22 s (default joint speeds, generous approaches) |
| Expected after optimisation | ≈ 7–14 s (reordered targets, faster joints, short approach/retract) |

One robot meets takt with large margin; the assessed skill is the optimisation
*method* and the guarding-distance calculation, not a capacity shortfall. Flag
cycle times that are physically implausible (joint speeds cranked past limits).

## Metrology labs

- **Linear and Angular Measuring Instruments — least-count problems** (use the
  corrected sheet in `LabInstructions/Quality_Labs/fixed/`): caliper — main-scale
  division 1 mm, 10 vernier divisions = 9 main divisions → **0.1 mm**. Micrometer
  — 1 mm barrel graduations, 50 thimble divisions per 1 mm → **0.02 mm** without
  the vernier; five vernier divisions = six thimble divisions → **0.004 mm** with
  it.
- **Groove Angle (V-Block):** included angle
  α = 2 sin⁻¹[ (d₂ − d₁) / (2(h₂ − h₁) − (d₂ − d₁)) ], *d* = roller diameter,
  *h* = height from the plate to the top of the roller. A standard V-block should
  come out near 90°.
- **Sine bar:** sin θ = h / L (θ is the taper's **half**-angle; whole angle = 2θ).
  Sensitivity: dθ = dh / (L cos θ), so error grows with θ.
- **Calibration:** deviation = reading − standard at every check size; accuracy
  over the range = the largest deviation; compare with the *published* accuracy.

## Statistical quality-control labs

- **Statistics with Excel** — processing times (n = 12): mean 6.19, median 6.2,
  mode 6.2, range 3.7, population variance 1.279, sample variance 1.395,
  population SD 1.131, sample SD 1.181. Waiting times (n = 50): mean 30.88, median
  30.45, two modes (31.8 and 28.5), histogram counts for the ten worksheet cells
  8, 8, 7, 6, 8, 4, 4, 2, 2, 1 — right-skewed, not a clean normal curve.
- **Variable control charts** (n = 10): A₂ = 0.308, B₃ = 0.284, B₄ = 1.716,
  D₃ = 0.223, D₄ = 1.777. Limits: X̄̄ ± A₂R̄; D₄R̄ / D₃R̄; B₄S̄ / B₃S̄. Use the
  corrected sheet (rules aligned with Chapter 10).
- **Attribute control charts** (n = 50): p̄ ± 3√(p̄(1 − p̄)/n); np̄ ± 3√(np̄(1 − p̄));
  a negative LCL is set to 0. Complementary tool: a Pareto chart.
- **Process capability:** Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ); Cpk = min[(USL − X̄)/(3σ),
  (X̄ − LSL)/(3σ)]; capable if ≥ 1.33; USL 0.5008, LSL 0.4992 in; σ = R̄/d₂
  (d₂ = 2.326) or STDEV.P. Cpk ≤ Cp, and Cpk is the off-centre index.
- **Gauge R&R (5.15σ convention; corrected sheet):** EV = 5.15 R̄/1.128;
  AV = √((5.15 X̄diff/K)² − EV²/(n r)) with K = d₂\* = 1.91 (3 operators) or 1.41
  (2 operators), n = 5 parts, r = 2 trials (n r = 10); Vp = 5.15 Rp/2.48 (five
  parts). **Part B key:** average ranges 6.44 and 6.46; EV ≈ 29.4; AV = 0 (the
  root is negative); R&R ≈ 29.4; Vp ≈ 82.2; Vt ≈ 87.3; **%R&R ≈ 34 %** —
  unacceptable. (With the original sheet's 3.18 and ÷ 40 the answer is ≈ 42 %,
  which is why the sheet was corrected.)

## Materials-testing labs

- **Hardness:** the annealed specimen scatters more than the hardened one (soft,
  coarse, multi-phase structure). Rockwell C 51 ≈ Brinell 500 and Rockwell B 85 ≈
  Brinell 165 — i.e. roughly equal, check against your chart.
- **Tensile / microhardness:** effective case depth at HRC 50, true case depth at
  HRC 40 (template definition); stress = load ÷ original area; strain = extension
  ÷ original length; toughness = area under the curve.
- **Charpy:** seven test temperatures (about −60, −40, −20, 0 °C, room, 60,
  100 °C); DBTT read from the transition of each curve; low-temperature fracture
  granular/flat, high-temperature fibrous with necking; body-centred cubic
  structures are the ones that turn brittle in the cold.

|------------|-----|-----|-----|-------|-------|

# Rubric quick reference (default plan, then the other catalogue labs)

Each lab is out of the marks shown; the machine-learning capstone (ML Weeks 3–6)
also carries a 100-point rubric reproduced at the end.

**Logic Thinking (Rocksi) (10)**: Sequencing 1 · Loops 2 · Conditionals 2 ·
Pick-and-place sequence 2 · Simulated I/O 1 · Optimisation challenge 1 ·
Reflection 1. *Award loop/conditional marks for explanation, not just level
completion.*

**Design documentation (5)**: Specification sheet(s) 1 · BOM for one kit
1 · Task list / process-flow chart 1 · Project schedule + Gantt 1 · Facility
layout + HSE risk assessment 1. *Look for traceability — every document describes
the same cell and kit.*

**Facility design & AnyLogic (10)**: Facility drawing 4 · Run 1 analysis
2 · Run 2 analysis 2 · Run 3 analysis 2 · Run 4 analysis 2 (confirm the split;
handout implies drawing 4 + analysis 1.5 × 4). *Analysis must cite the specific
statistic that moved and the case-study consequence.*

**Lean VSM (10)**: Current-state VSM (boxes with C/T, C/O, uptime, batch;
WIP triangles; information flow; totalled lead-time ladder) 3 · Takt + operator
balance chart + bottleneck named with the gap quantified 2 · Seven-wastes
classification + PCE computed and interpreted 2 · Push / pull / supermarket runs
with WIP and lead time recorded, interpretation consistent with the numbers 2 ·
Future-state VSM with one SMED + one pull change, reduction justified against the
ladder 1. *AI not permitted for the map or the takt/PCE arithmetic. Check the
ladder actually totals to the quoted numbers.*

**Ergonomics (10)**: Procedure followed, all three tasks assessed 1 ·
REBA scoring — correct Table A/B/C lookups, coupling and activity adjustments,
final score and risk band for each of the three tasks 4 · Sources of error and
limitations — at least three specific sources, advantage/limitation and a
proposed improvement, references the Chapter 7 risk factors 4 · Conclusion +
controls ordered by the hierarchy of controls 1.

**SPC & Gauge R&R (10)**: 90 readings, blinded and in the randomised
order, all 10 parts × 3 trials per operator 2 · Gauge R&R — EV, AV, GRR, PV, TV,
%GRR and ndc all reported and internally consistent 3 · Bias in mm + a linearity
statement vs the reference values 1 · X̄/R chart read correctly, every Western
Electric rule break listed and named, Cpk reported and compared to 1.33 3 ·
Reflection — acceptability judged against the %GRR and ndc bands, effect of gauge
error on Cpk reasoned through, release decision stated 1. *AI not permitted for
readings or calculations. Identical values across operators/trials means the
study was not read blind.*

**ML Week 1 (10)**: `prompts.md` — five prompts rewritten with all five
R-C-T-C-F elements present 3 · FMEA summarised at three audiences —
audience-appropriate and technically accurate 2 · Hallucination hunt — a
fabrication documented, with evidence of how it was verified 3 · `spc_starter.py`
runs, is commented, and the student can explain it on request 2. *Exercise 3
needs genuine verification evidence (empty ASTM search, "no results" screenshot),
not "I think this is made up".*

**ML Week 2 (10)**: Week 1 code runs against the real dataset 1 · All
five data-quality issues found; `quality_log` complete (row_index, column,
original, corrected, reason, action); the days 43–47 special cause correctly
**kept, not deleted** 4 · X̄ chart with correct control limits — `sigma /
sqrt(n)`, not the std of daily means 3 · Cpk against USL 25.050 / LSL 24.950, in
the expected 1.1–1.2 range and interpreted 1 · Reflection 1. *Deduct for silent
row deletion even if the final chart is right.*

**ML Week 3 (progress check; rolled into the capstone rubric)**: data
loaded and labelled, 7×3 sensor plot produced, constant sensors identified,
correlations computed, reflection answered.

**ML Week 4 (capstone rubric — Working Predictive Model 30, Code
Quality 20)**: biggest scoring risk is `train_test_split` instead of a manual
engine-wise split — symptom is RMSE 5–8 cycles. Make students diagnose it via the
Task 3 assert.

**ML Week 5 (capstone rubric — Streamlit Application 25, Documentation &
Honest Disclosure 15)**: deliverable is a public URL that loads and predicts.

**ML Week 6 (capstone rubric — Week 6 Presentation 10; carries the full
100-point capstone rubric for ML Weeks 3–6)** — see the table at the end.

**TPM/OEE & RCA (10)**: OEE computed correctly (availability,
performance, quality shown separately); every log entry attributed to a Big Loss;
largest loss named 2 · Failure-mode Pareto correct (descending bars, cumulative
line); vital few identified; RNF discussed 1 · 5-Why chain + six-bone Ishikawa
with measured feature evidence on the bones 2 · Classifier built via LLM
direction; confusion matrix + precision/recall reported; class-imbalance trap
identified and explained; accuracy correctly rejected 4 · D4/D5 tie feature
importances to the fishbone and propose a TPM-executable corrective action 1.

**RoboDK work cell (10)**: jogging in joint/linear/tool coordinates,
singularity and joint-limit behaviour recorded 1 · kitting cell built, every
pick/place verified inside the reach envelope, the binding reach limit and layout
change recorded 2 · working pick-and-place program with targets and gripper I/O,
runs, cycle time reported 3 · cycle time compared against the Lean-lab takt, one
round of optimisation with improved time and gap quantified 3 · minimum
safeguarding distance computed from a stated stopping time, a specific Chapter 6
safeguard chosen and justified 1. *If the student's Lean-lab takt was wrong, mark
Task 4 on method against a takt you supply.*

## Machine-learning capstone rubric — ML Weeks 3–6 (100 points)

| Category | Points | 27–30 / top band |
|----------|:------:|------------------|
| Working predictive model | 30 | Validation RMSE ≤ 22 cycles; beats naive ≥ 2×; engine-wise split verified with assert; RUL clipped at 125 |
| Code quality | 20 | Clean, commented; rolling features grouped by engine; random seed set; `feature_cols` saved with the model |
| Streamlit application | 25 | Public URL loads; handles CSV upload; RUL colour-coded; sensor-trend plot; bad input handled gracefully |
| Documentation & honest disclosure | 15 | "About this model" states data source and limits; actual validation RMSE; ≥ 2 explicit "not suitable for" statements; sample input provided |
| Week 6 presentation | 10 | Live demo works; one technical decision explained clearly; handles 2–3 questions; one specific limitation stated |

LLM policy for the capstone: using LLMs to write, debug and understand code is
required and encouraged, but a student who cannot explain a non-trivial submitted
block in the ML Week 6 presentation loses up to 20 points across all categories.

# Known failure modes and fallbacks

Extends the pattern in the Logic Thinking (Rocksi) instructor notes: every browser lab depends on a
third-party site that could be blocked or down on the day.

| Lab | Most likely failure | Fallback |
|-----|--------------------|----------|
| Logic Thinking (Rocksi) | Rocksi blocked by the firewall / site down | Screenshot walk-through slides; mark from the quiz answers |
| Design Documentation | Microsoft Project or Visio missing from the Office image | Draw the Gantt / GA in Excel or Word; do not penalise tool choice |
| Facility Design & Simulation | AnyLogic PLE install missing or the demo model over the size limit | Instructor runs the model on the projector; students analyse the shared screenshots |
| Lean VSM | AnyLogic Cloud model won't run public, or draw.io blocked | Supply pre-run push/pull/supermarket numbers; students still do the VSM on paper and the takt/PCE in Sheets |
| Ergonomics (REBA) | Task video/photo sets not staged on FOL or won't play | Instructor plays the clips from a laptop/projector; students score from the shared screen |
| Virtual Caliper | webR cells slow to load or a student's browser blocks them | **No external dependency** — worst case is a slow first load; have the answer key so a group that runs out of time can still complete the analysis from a partial reading set. Never add `library(ggplot2)` to fix a rendering issue |
| ML Week 1 | Claude.ai / ChatGPT / Colab blocked | Any free LLM the college allows; the exercise is prompt structure, not a specific model |
| ML Week 2 | `spc_data.csv` not staged, or Colab upload fails | Have the CSV on a USB / shared drive; students can also run locally if Python is present |
| ML Week 3 | UCI/Kaggle sign-in wall during the lab | Host `train_FD001.txt` on FOL yourself — do not rely on Kaggle at lab time |
| ML Week 4 | RMSE < 10 cycles (row-wise split data leak) | This is the teaching moment, not a failure — make the student find it via the Task 3 assert |
| ML Week 5 | Streamlit deploy fails: model > 50 MB or `requirements.txt` conflict | Retrain with `n_estimators=50`; use the pinned versions in the lab text; `pyngrok` from Colab for a temporary URL |
| ML Week 6 | A student's deployment is down at presentation time | Instructor's reference app on the projector; the student still defends their technical decision and limitations |
| TPM/OEE | `archive.ics.uci.edu` unreachable; or team reuses C-MAPSS code that doesn't fit tabular data | FOL fallback copy of AI4I 2020; the C-MAPSS-code red flag means mark down the "transfer" criterion |
| Robotic Work-Cell Design | `web.robodk.com` blocked at home for a student; station file won't reload | Extended deadline (it is already a 3-week take-home); accept a screen recording made on any machine where it does load |
| Metrology / quality-control labs | Instruments or gauge blocks missing; bearings or beads short; worksheet constants wrong | Post the corrected sheets from `Quality_Labs/fixed/`; share instruments in a rotation; run the Excel part from a class data set if measuring runs out of time |
| Materials rotation | **Dry ice not delivered** for the Charpy station | Order two weeks ahead for all three weeks; if a delivery fails, run Charpy on the room-temperature and hot-water points only, or swap that week's group to another station and repeat Charpy later |
| Materials rotation | A tester is down (Rockwell/Brinell, tensile machine, pendulum) | Instructor runs the test and shares the raw data with the group; each student still writes their own report |
| Virtual Welding | Simulator won't start / WPS booklet missing | Power on early (2+ min boot); keep the WPSs on FOL as well as in the booklet; rotate students across working units |

**General:** walk the §10 checklist from the college network the day before each
lab, and keep this table updated with whatever actually broke this term.

# Choosing and scheduling labs

Pick labs to fit your course, your background and your equipment — most stand
alone. Plan around the three groups that do not:

- **The machine-learning labs are a set — they cannot be cherry-picked.** Six
  consecutive weeks, in order (each week's output is the next week's input, and the
  capstone rubric spans four of the six). Deliver all six or none.
- **The three materials labs are a 3-week rotation** (§13). All three run every week,
  so none can be delivered alone.
- **Dependencies:** Facility Design & Simulation needs Engineering Design Process
  Documentation first; Robotic Work-Cell Design needs the Lean VSM takt time;
  ML Week 2 follows ML Week 1 (and ideally the Virtual Caliper); TPM/OEE, Root
  Cause & a New Dataset follows the machine-learning set; the later Virtual Welding
  labs are best after the first one.

The student book's *Teacher preparation* chapter section carries the same rules
and the per-lab room / equipment matrix.

---

# Materials-testing rotation and dry ice

Split the class into three groups; each group starts at a different lab and moves
on every week:

| | Week 1 | Week 2 | Week 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Group A** | Hardness | Tensile and Microhardness | Charpy |
| **Group B** | Tensile and Microhardness | Charpy | Hardness |
| **Group C** | Charpy | Hardness | Tensile and Microhardness |

- **Dry ice is needed in all three weeks** (one group is at the Charpy station each
  week). **The lab technician needs two weeks' notice** to order it for the
  three-week block — give them the three dates and agree the quantity per session
  **[confirm]**.
- Staff the Charpy station for the whole period (cold bath, dry ice, swinging
  pendulum). Safety glasses and safety footwear for everyone in the materials lab.
- Post the group list and the rotation on FOL before week 1 so each group prepares
  for its starting lab. Tests are done in teams; **reports are individual**.

# FOL quiz staging

`python R/gen_lab_quizzes.py` writes one Brightspace question-import CSV **per lab**
into `quizzes/` (gitignored — stage on FOL, do not commit), named by lab, e.g.
`logic-rocksi_quiz.csv`, `gauge-rr_quiz.csv`, `weld-t-lap_quiz.csv`. Each quiz is out
of 10, all Written Response, with attachments switched on where a file is asked for.
Create the quiz in FOL, import the CSV, then save as CSV UTF-8 if you edit it.

| Group | Quiz files |
|-------|-----------|
| Default plan | `logic-rocksi`, `design-documentation`, `facility-anylogic`, `lean-vsm`, `ergonomics-reba`, `virtual-caliper`, `ml-week1-ai-literacy`, `ml-week2-data-spc`, `ml-week3-cmapss`, `ml-week4-model`, `ml-week5-deploy`, `ml-week6-capstone`, `tpm-oee-rca`, `robodk-work-cell` |
| Metrology | `instruments`, `v-groove`, `sine-bar`, `calibration` |
| Quality control | `excel-stats`, `variable-charts`, `attribute-charts`, `capability`, `gauge-rr` |
| Materials | `hardness`, `tensile-microhardness`, `charpy-dbtt` |
| Virtual welding | `weld-flat-single`, `weld-flat-multi`, `weld-groove-single`, `weld-groove-multi`, `weld-t-lap`, `weld-vertical-t` |

The metrology and quality-control quizzes point students to corrected worksheets;
post the copies in `LabInstructions/Quality_Labs/fixed/` (they fix the Cp/Cpk
wording, the R&R constants, the least-count problems and the control-chart rules).
The welding quizzes replace the source PDF sheets, which had copy-paste slips.
